raw_recipe.headline: Thousand Island Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Thousand Island dressing is a simple recipe with mayonnaise, ketchup, and sweet pickle relish. It is easy to make and customize to your liking.
raw_recipe.name: Thousand Island Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together mayonnaise, relish, ketchup, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until thoroughly combined, and serve.

review.reviewBody: My recipe is very similar but I add 3 boiled eggs finely chopping and instead of salt and pepper, about 2 tsp Lawry's seasoning salt to counter balance the sweetness of the pickle relish. Also, I use bread and butter pickles sometimes instead of the sweet pickle relish and it gives it an extra good taste. Bear in mind, the more ketchup you use, the sweeter it will be as ketchup contains more sugar than most people realize. I suggest adding a little bit of ketchup at a time tasting as you go. Enjoy!
The trick to really kick up this recipe is to NOT use relish - instead, cut up very finely sweet gerkin pickles and use in place of the relish.

I only made half of the recipe since I am the only one who likes thousand island. I thought it was a little too sweet and needed a little something else. So I added a tsp apple cider vinegar and 1/4 tsp onion powder. Now I think it is just perfect.

It's okay but I've found half sweet and half dill relish, a tsp of lemon juice, a tsp of Worcestershire sauce, and paprika to taste makes it taste more like the commercial dressing. I don't add salt or pepper. I do add horseradish to taste to mine to give it a bit of depth and zing!

A pretty good recipe, but a bit sweet for my taste. I cut the sweet relish to 2/3 cup and added 2 tablespoons of real crumbled bacon, 1/4 teaspoon liquid smoke and 1/4 teaspoon hot sauce (I prefer Cholula). That was a big hit!

This is very similar to mine. I add diced onion and garlic and let it meld in the fridge preferably overnight but at least an hour before serving. I also use both dill and sweet relish, sometimes bread and butter relish, but only about half of your recipe.
Next time I will cut back on the ketchup and reduce size of the pickle relish. Also, for a retired couple, we can easily cut the recipe in half for a more reasonable amount produced

Really good and simple as is. Perfect for making Reuben sandwiches. I cut recipe in half. Started adding 1 tsp. Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 tsp mustard powder to cut a little of the sweetness as one reviewer suggested. Will also try adding a little lemon juice or vinegar next time. Did that. Try adding only vinegar next time.
easy and good. I wanted a little spicy so I used chili sauce instead of ketchup and a sprinkle of paprika. wonderful
Quick & easy. I also add 1 tsp of white vinegar, a Tbsp of sugar, & 4 chopped hard boiled eggs. Can add 1tsp of worchshire too if you'd like. Good base recipe!

I've made this so many times just as written and it's a big hit. Yesterday I made it using 1/2 Dukes and 1/2 Kewpie mayonnaise which gave it a slightly less sweet flavor and omitted the salt (personal preference since the kewpie has msg). I also found myself out of sweet pickle relish, so I minced up some Famous Dave's Sweet and Spicy pickle chips. A favorite recipe is now even better according to my husband.

I made the recipe exactly as it was listed (shocker, I never do that), but I was in a hurry and wanted to get a good idea how it tasted before I made changes. I cook organic so everything that went into this recipe was organic with the exception of the sweet pickle relish. I loved Vlasic but I can't find it any longer so I had to learn to like Heinz (it isn't as sweet as Vlasic). Honestly other than cutting the recipe in half (I am the only one that eats Thousand Island) I wouldn't change a thing. It wasn't to sweet, it had a nice balance. I cranked it out in less than 5 minutes, tossed it in the fridge for about 5 minutes and while cool it wasn't cold and it was still good. Can't wait until tomorrow to see how the flavors meld after it has had time rest and chill. Better than any store bought I have found. Very pleased.
Excellent Thousand Island for taco salad. Quick, simple, and very tasty, Thank you!
Growing up my Dad loved this dressing, the one thing I remember him using capers but I think that was in place of pickle relish? Unfortunately he is deceased so no answer

A really good recipe, like old fashioned Thousand Island dressing. I tinkered with it a bit, and like it better after I added a dash more mayonnaise, and reduced the amount of sweet relish. I also used a seasoned pepper melange blend which is really good!
we made this when I was a child with a little els pickle relish and only with Miracle Whip. It has more tang than mayonnaise. always loved it!!

Had to find a recipe quick because my Ruben's were finished except that my store bought dressing was horrible. Found this recipe, made it and served it and it was a hit. So simple and easy, yet so flavorful. Won't ever buy from a store again. I have my go-to recipe. Thanks
Good. Use chili sauce instead of ketchup; add 1 diced hard boiled egg, onion , relish and celery. 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce. 1 teaspoon garlic and pepper.
I used dill relish and added a little pickle juice, 2 dash of Worcestershire sauce and 2 dash lemon juice.
I added a touch of horseradish and that elevated the dressing to a whole ‘nother level.
